Article Title: DailyObjects launches artist collection of iPhone 18 cases featuring works by five artists
Article Text:
Original art meets everyday technology

Five artists, five creative narratives

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Company sees demand for more personal accessories

Pricing and availability

Design-led lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has launched The Artist Collection, a new range of MagSafe-compatible iPhone cases that brings original artwork from five Indian and international artists to everyday accessories.Built around the theme "The Art. The Artist. The Object.", the collection aims to transform smartphone cases into a medium for artistic expression. The launch features exclusive artwork created by artists Amrit Pal Singh, Kafeel Ahmed Ansari, Hey Mady, Mercedes Bazan (Mechibaz), and Yash Pradhan.According to DailyObjects, the initiative is designed to make original art more accessible by integrating it into products people use every day. Rather than relying on licensed imagery or generic decorative designs, the company said the collection focuses on artist-led creations developed specifically for smartphone cases. The brand said each artist brings a distinct creative perspective, with themes ranging from nostalgia and popular culture to urban life, cultural heritage, love and symbols of luck from different parts of the world.One of the collections, "Once Upon A Toy" by Amrit Pal Singh, reimagines well-known figures from history, literature and popular culture through his signature Toy Faces style.The series includes interpretations of characters such as Dracula, Frankenstein, Sherlock Holmes, Cleopatra, Medusa, Marie Antoinette, Vincent Van Gogh and Alice in Wonderland.Kafeel Ahmed Ansari's "In the Name of Love" collection draws inspiration from hand-painted Indian commercial art. Featuring bold colours, typography and floral motifs, the artwork explores different expressions of love through a visual language influenced by Bollywood and Indian street culture.Hey Mady's "Around the World" collection focuses on eight global cities including Mumbai, Tokyo, Paris, New York, Hong Kong, London, Seoul and Shanghai. Instead of iconic landmarks, the illustrations highlight everyday details and personal experiences associated with urban life.Meanwhile, Mercedes Bazan, known as Mechibaz, presents "Pretty Powerful", a series that combines anime-inspired characters with traditional Indian jewellery to explore themes of identity, heritage and self-expression.Yash Pradhan's "Signs of Fortune" collection draws on symbols of luck from different cultures, including Japan's Maneki-neko, Ireland's Four-Leaf Clover, Turkey's Evil Eye and Sweden's Dala Horse, reinterpreting them through colourful and detailed artwork.Commenting on the launch, Pankaj Garg, Co-founder and CEO of DailyObjects, said consumers increasingly want products that feel individual and curated rather than mass-produced. "A phone case is one of the most personal everyday objects people carry. It travels with them everywhere and can become a reflection of their personality through the art they choose," he said.The Artist Collection has been designed for compatible models across the iPhone 16, iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 series, excluding Duo models. DailyObjects said Kafeel Ahmed Ansari's collection will be available exclusively for the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. All cases support MagSafe functionality and are priced at Rs 1,499. The company said the collection will roll out in phases, with all five artist collections expected to be available by early December 2026 through the DailyObjects website, mobile app and Exclusive Brand Outlets across India.
Article Summary: DailyObjects has launched The Artist Collection, a new range of MagSafe- compatible iPhone cases. The collection brings original artwork from five Indian and international artists to everyday accessories. The launch features exclusive artwork created by artists Amrit Pal Singh, Kafeel Ahmed Ansari, Hey Mady, Mercedes Bazan and Yash Pradhan.

Article Title: Back to work after Diwali? 7 ways ChatGPT can help you clear your inbox, organise tasks and catch up on pending projects
Article Text:
ChatGPT

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Returning to work after Diwali can mean more than just getting back to your routine. An overflowing inbox, pending approvals, back-to-back meetings and unfinished projects can make the first few days particularly hectic. With several tasks competing for attention, figuring out where to start can be a challenge. ChatGPT can help make the transition easier by summarising work updates, prioritising pending tasks, organising schedules and picking up projects left unfinished before the festive break. Here are seven ways to use ChatGPT to make your post-Diwali return to work less overwhelming.1. First things first: What did you miss while you were away?Before replying to the first email in your inbox, it helps to understand what actually happened while you were gone. With ChatGPT's app plugins, you can bring together relevant emails, documents and project updates to understand what's changed. Instead of working through individual threads, ask for a briefing organised by project, with the important decisions, outstanding requests and deadlines highlighted.Try asking: "I've been away for the Diwali break from [date] to [date]. Go through my work emails and relevant project documents from the past week.Tell me what changed while I was away, which decisions were made, what needs my response and which deadlines are coming up. Organise it by project and keep it concise."2. Everything looks urgent. But what actually needs to get done today?Once you've caught up, the next challenge is deciding what deserves your attention. There's a presentation due tomorrow, a colleague waiting for an approval, a report due Friday, and three requests marked urgent. They can't all be first on the list. Use ChatGPT to weigh deadlines, dependencies and impact, rather than just sorting tasks by when they arrived.Try asking: "Here's my list of pending work and deadlines. Help me prioritise it based on urgency, impact and whether someone else is waiting on my response to proceed. Identify the urgent things I should finish today, what I can schedule for later this week and anything that needs clarification before I begin."3. Your calendar has other plans for your week back.Just as you've figured out your priorities, you notice the back-to-back meetings on your calendar. There's barely an hour to get through the work you've just identified, let alone prepare for the discussions. You can review upcoming meetings alongside your priorities and find available time to focus. ChatGPT can also help you prepare for important conversations by pulling together the relevant context and suggesting questions or talking points.Try asking: "Look at my calendar for the next week and the priorities I've identified. Help me find realistic time to complete them, flag meetings I need to prepare for and suggest a plan that leaves room for unexpected requests."4. That half-finished presentation waiting for vendor inputs isn't going to finish itself.There was a proposal that was almost ready, a presentation waiting for final numbers or a project that needed one last round of feedback before the holidays. Returning to it now can mean spending an hour simply remembering what you'd already done.This is where Projects in ChatGPT can be useful. Keep related chats, reference files and project instructions together so you can return to the same body of work without reconstructing the context each time. You can ask ChatGPT to review earlier drafts, identify what's changed from conversations through the week and update the placeholders.Try asking: "I'm picking up this presentation after the festive break. Review the earlier draft, feedback and reference documents in this Project. Tell me what's complete, what's missing, look through vendor responses and update the placeholders. Help me work through the remaining sections one by one without changing the parts we've already finalized."5. For the approvals, reminders and conversations that went quiet.By this point, you've probably found a few loose ends. A vendor was meant to send revised costs, a colleague hasn't reviewed a document, and a client is waiting for a response. None is particularly difficult on its own, but together they can consume a surprising part of the day. You can work across apps to review relevant conversations and prepare context-specific follow-ups. Rather than sending a generic reminder, ChatGPT can help identify what was last agreed, what's outstanding and what the other person needs to do next.Try asking: "Review the conversations related to these three projects. Identify any pending approvals, unanswered questions or promised updates. Draft a short follow-up for each, referencing the last discussion and making the next action clear."6. The work is moving again. Can you make the next few days easier?A common problem with returning from a break is that the first day gets spent catching up while the work across projects continues to proceed. To be on top of it all. ChatGPT can help with scheduled reminders and recurring check-ins. Set a recurring reminder to revisit an outstanding approval or schedule a daily prompt to review priorities, so that important next steps don't disappear beneath new requests.Try asking: "Remind me tomorrow morning to check whether the proposal has been approved, set an 8 AM update on open and moving items across projects and at 9 AM, draft a list of closures for me to review my top work priorities for the day."7. Finally, find your rhythm without trying to finish the entire week today.You've caught up on what happened, identified the urgent work, and put a few things back in motion. But after the festivities, getting back into the rhythm of work can still take a little effort.This is where ChatGPT Voice offers a different way to organise your thoughts. Rather than staring at another to-do list, talk through what's on your mind, the ideas you want to feed into a presentation and the brief you have to share with a vendor. ChatGPT can help build these out while you speak, so you have a working ground to play with.Try saying: “I have a presentation to finish and a brief to send to a vendor, but my thoughts are still all over the place after the Diwali break. Let me talk you through what I have in mind. Help me organise these ideas into a presentation outline and draft the vendor brief into a draft email as we go. Ask me questions where you need more detail, and help me refine both as I think of changes.”
Article Summary: ChatGPT can help make the transition easier by summarising work updates, prioritising pending tasks, organising schedules and picking up projects left unfinished before the festive break. Here are seven ways to use ChatGPT to make your post-Diwali return to work less overwhelming.

Article Title: The Claude payday: How Anthropic’s IPO could make thousands of staff millionaires
Article Text:
Representative Image

How Anthropic employee stock awards gained value

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Where the wealth could go

Anthropic launched its IPO this week, bringing the company’s market value to nearly $1.3 trillion by the end of its first day of trading. Shares of the Claude maker closed at $97.17 on first day (November 19), about 17% above the $83 offering price. The Nasdaq debut also gave employees a public market price for the stock awards they received as part of their pay.At the $83 offering price, CNBC estimated that employee equity was worth about $232 billion on paper, or roughly $44 million per employee across a workforce of 5,300. Early hires who accumulated more shares stand to gain more. Investors told CNBC that at least 400 early employees could each hold equity worth $100 million or more at that price. The exact number of staff whose holdings are worth at least $1 million remains unclear.Anthropic’s prospectus listed outstanding options covering about 1.77 billion shares, with a weighted-average exercise price of $2.91. An option gives its holder the right to buy a share at a preset price. At the $83 offering price, an option with that average exercise price was worth about $80 per share before taxes. The filing also listed more than 1 billion shares tied to restricted stock units that had not yet met service-based vesting conditions at the time of the listing.Vesting schedules determine when employees gain rights to their stock awards, and lockup agreements can delay when they can sell. How much employees ultimately receive will depend on how many shares they can sell, the price at the time and the taxes they owe.Redfin estimated that the combined post-IPO equity wealth of current and former Anthropic employees would be enough to buy 9% of San Francisco’s homes. CNBC reported that brokers expect some employees to borrow against their shares to buy property.Some of the equity could also go to charity. Under Anthropic’s donation matching programme, employees hired before May 17, 2024, can pledge up to half of their vested shares for a three-to-one company match. Employees hired on or after that date can pledge up to a quarter of their vested shares for a one-to-one match.
Article Summary: Anthropic launched its IPO this week, bringing the company’s market value to nearly $1.3 trillion by the end of its first day of trading. Shares of the Claude maker closed at $97.17 on first day (November 19), about 17% above the $83 offering price.

Article Title: Days after telling Apple CEO, 'great doing business with you', Meta’s AI chief Alexandr Wang takes a dig at iPhone maker; says: Yet another...

Mark Zuckerberg 'thanks note' to Apple

When Alexandr Wang said 'mommy and daddy playing nice' on Apple partnership

Meta’s AI chief Alexandr Wang is back at doing what many may say he is a regular at doing, which is making fun of competition. Meta AI Lab head Wang has often made fun of Google, or Google Gemini, to be precise on Twitter. His latest target is iPhone maker Apple . Quoting a rumour claiming that 'Apple reportedly is building a new AI agent similar to Meta’s Muse', Wang took a dig at Apple. Replying to the speculation post on X, formerly Twitter, Wang wrote, "you already know these corposlops are about to unleash yet another butthole on us".Incidentally, Wang's potshot at Apple comes just days after he complimented Apple and Apple CEO John Ternus for a partnership, "great doing business with you john apple 🍎🤝," wrote Wang. Meta AI head wrote the same quoting a post from Ternus that said, "Congrats to the team! Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open's caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!"Wang thanked Apple after the two companies announced a partnership last month. What makes the collaboration important is that Apple and Facebook-parent Meta have spent years trading barbs at each other. The companies have taken digs at each other openly over privacy and the future of computing. Meta recently released its Muse Spark Open, a model that the company claims is the most powerful US-developed open-weight AI model available.In layman terms, Muse Spark Open is an open-weights AI model, which means developers can understand how it works and customize it to their needs.As proof of Muse Spark Open's capabilities, Meta said that it worked with Apple to make the model run locally across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Meta's model will be free to download, with a license allowing commercial use, and will also be available through cloud providers and developer tools.Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg too sent a rare public 'thanks note' to Apple, and he did by name. In a post on X, he wrote, "runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple." Apple CEO Ternus replied, "Congrats to the team! Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open's caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!"Talking about the partnership with Axios, Wang said, "We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again." While Wang acknowledged that Apple and Meta will continue to compete in some areas, he said that this does not have to prevent the two companies from working together. "Where it makes sense to collaborate and partner, we want to be able to do so," he said.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang has often made fun of Google, or Google Gemini, to be precise. His latest target is iPhone maker Apple. Wang's potshot at Apple comes just days after he complimented Apple and Apple CEO John Ternus for a partnership.

Article Title: Anthropic founder to join Michael Dell, who pledged $6.25 billion, in donating to Trump Accounts
Article Text:
Warming ties between Anthropic and the Trump administration

What are Trump Accounts and how much Dell CEO has pledged

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown plans to contribute to US President Donald Trump’s cradle-to-adulthood investment program, known as Trump Accounts, news agency Reuters reported citing a source familiar with the matter. The move places Brown among a growing list of wealthy donors, including Michael Dell, who previously pledged $6.25 billion, backing the federal initiative. The planned donation comes right on the heels of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering, where the artificial intelligence (AI) company raised $93.5 billion after underwriters exercised an option to purchase additional shares.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent hinted at the contribution during an interview with CNBC on Friday (November 20), noting that an Anthropic founder would be donating to the initiative “over the next few weeks,” though he did not name Brown directly.Brown’s contribution marks the latest step in Anthropic’s broader push to mend fences with the White House. In the past, the AI developer and its CEO, Dario Amodei, have occasionally clashed with Trump and senior officials over AI policy. In recent months, however, both sides have shown clear signs of moving toward a smoother working relationship:Serving as Anthropic’s chief compute officer, Brown has stepped forward as a primary bridge to the administration, attending a US-hosted G20 technology event in August as well as the September rollout of a government AI tool.Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Trump stated that he has “a lot of respect” for Amodei, signaling a noticeable thaw in relations between the president and the AI giant.Designed to encourage investing and build financial literacy from childhood, the Trump Accounts program provides government-funded investment accounts worth $1,000 to US citizens born between 2025 and 2028.Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, are now the single largest private backers of Trump Accounts, the new US government investment accounts for children. Their $6.25 billion pledge puts $250 into the accounts of 25 million American kids aged 10 and under, and the couple said earlier this month that the full amount would be deposited within days.It is the biggest gift the Dells have ever made, more than double what their foundation gave away in its first 26 years. Most of their giving before this stayed in Texas, where Michael Dell started his company from a University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) dorm room in 1984. In April, the couple became the first donors to cross $1 billion in lifetime giving to the university, with a $750 million commitment for a new medical campus.
Article Summary: Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown plans to contribute to US President Donald Trump’s cradle-to-adulthood investment program. The move places Brown among a growing list of wealthy donors, including Michael Dell, who previously pledged $6.25 billion, backing the federal initiative.

Article Title: Meta threatens to pull WhatsApp from Canada; tells government: Your demands ignore software realities
Article Text:
Why technology companies are upset with Bill C-22

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta has warned Canadian lawmakers that it may consider pulling encrypted services from the country if the federal government passes its proposed lawful access legislation without further amendments. Speaking before a Senate committee reviewing Bill C-22, company representatives this week argued that the draft law would force technology companies to compromise digital security in order to comply with police warrants.Bill C-22, which passed the House of Commons in June, requires electronic service providers to adapt their systems so that they can hand over user data to investigators upon request. Critics say the mandate directly threatens end-to-end encryption, which is the security standard used by platforms like WhatsApp , Facebook, and Instagram to ensure messages can only be read by the sender and recipient."Ultimately, the Canadian government would be enforcing and imposing a law that it is not technically feasible to comply with and still offer secure, end-to-end encrypted services to Canadians," Robyn Greene, Meta’s director of privacy and public policy, testified before senators, according to a report in CBC.When pressed on whether the company would withdraw products from the Canadian market if the bill becomes law, Rachel Curran, Meta’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would have to "review all of our options."Curran previously told Bloomberg that weakening encryption is a "red line" for Meta, warning the legislation risks turning private companies into "an arm of the government's surveillance apparatus. "The standoff centers on Part 2 of Bill C-22, which grants ministers the authority to issue confidential orders compelling tech companies to build law enforcement access capabilities into their platforms. The provision also allows the government to require companies to retain customer metadata—including IP addresses and connection logs—for up to six months.While Ottawa introduced amendments barring orders that create a "systemic vulnerability," tech leaders and cybersecurity experts contend the language is overly vague. Cryptographers and privacy advocates have long maintained that it is impossible to build a "backdoor" exclusively for police without leaving that same entry point exposed to cybercriminals and foreign intelligence agencies.The primary flashpoint is Part 2 of the bill, which grants ministers in the country the authority to issue confidential orders forcing service providers to build interception capabilities for police. The legislation also empowers the government to require companies to retain sensitive customer metadata—including IP addresses and connection logs—for up to six months.While Ottawa introduced amendments prohibiting orders that create a "systemic vulnerability," tech leaders and cryptographers argue the language is dangerously vague. Security experts maintain that creating a "backdoor" for law enforcement inevitably creates a weak point that malicious hackers and foreign spies will eventually exploit.Meta is far from alone in its opposition, joining a broad coalition of tech giants, privacy-focused apps, and digital rights advocates pushing back against the draft law. Both Google and Apple have issued warnings that Bill C-22 threatens customer security and could break end-to-end encryption.Encrypted messaging platform Signal too has stated that it would leave Canada rather than compromise its security protocols, while Toronto-based VPN provider Windscribe pledged to maintain its strict no-logs policy regardless of the bill's outcome.
Article Summary: Canadian lawmakers are considering Bill C-22, which would require electronic service providers to hand over user data to investigators. Critics say the mandate directly threatens end-to-end encryption, which is the security standard used by platforms like WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram.

Article Title: ‘Let Students Search’: Google employees want an AI-free option for schools, here’s why
Article Text:
‘Let Students Search’: Google workers want an AI-free option for schools, here’s why

What Google workers are asking for

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Can schools turn off AI inside Search

Hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking the company to give schools a version of Google Search without generative AI. The appeal comes as three of the largest US school districts weigh switching search engines, according to The New York Times. The issue is whether schools can turn off AI for students and still let them look things up on Google.The dispute began earlier this month when Google’s vice president for education, Chris Phillips, told the Times that Search and AI were “deeply integrated”. He said students attempting to use Search at schools that ban AI would see a message saying the service was unavailable. Some districts, including New York City, have already restricted student-facing generative AI over concerns about how it affects learning.New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of using its market power to push AI into public schools. In Chicago, parents, teachers and students protested outside a Google office. The Times subsequently reported that New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago were all considering alternative search engines.The Alphabet Workers Union’s petition, titled “Let Students Search”, is addressed to Phillips, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Search chief Elizabeth Hamon Reid. The union argues that educators should decide when students use AI and that taking away Search could prompt districts to drop other Google products.It also warned that losing school district business could affect job security.“The decision of how and when to implement AI into a classroom belongs to the educators leading it,” Parul Koul, the union’s president and a Google software engineer, said in a statement.Google has said that under changes expected early next year, schools will be able to enable or disable Search, Gemini and NotebookLM individually. That means a school could switch off the standalone Gemini chatbot and keep Search available to students. Google’s clarification left open whether schools could also disable the generative AI features that appear within Search itself.The union said some coverage had made it sound as though Google was deliberately punishing schools for opting out of AI. Its petition asks for a setting that would let schools apply their classroom AI policies to Search while keeping the search engine available for everyday use.
Article Summary: Hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking the company to give schools a version of Google Search without generative AI. The appeal comes as three of the largest US school districts weigh switching search engines. The issue is whether schools can turn off AI for students and still let them look things up on Google.

Article Title: A Meta employee asked Muse AI about the weather; It replied with bank balances
Article Text:
Where did the details come from?

What Meta says

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Meta employee was chatting with Muse about weather and tides when the AI agent brought up two bank balances. It named Capital One and Charles Schwab and gave amounts down to the cent. The employee said the accounts weren’t theirs, according to a Reuters investigation based on internal company posts.Other Meta employees reported receiving career advice they had never sought and seeing references to childcare requests they hadn’t made or products they hadn’t ordered. The incidents prompted some staff to raise concerns that Muse could be pulling information from conversations associated with other accounts.Another employee said Muse prompted her to reply to a message from her sister on Signal while she was using the AI agent on her personal phone. Signal uses end-to-end encryption. The employee said she hadn’t given Muse permission to access other apps and didn’t remember being asked to do so.“This seems like an extreme privacy violation,” the employee wrote in an internal post, according to Reuters.The incidents leave open a question about the source of the information.In the banking example, Muse presented the figures as the employee’s balances. It remains unclear whether they belonged to someone else or were generated by the AI. The Signal reminder also leaves open how Muse came up with the prompt.That distinction matters because a chat filled with somebody else’s information and a chat filled with invented details can look similar to the person reading it. The employee who asked about the weather had little to go on when Muse switched topics and presented the numbers as a personal update.A Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch that employee testing helps the company gather feedback, build safety and privacy protections and improve its products. The spokesperson also said staff have access to different versions of Muse and often test features and behaviour that people using the public app don’t encounter.The employee accounts describe what happened in those internal tests. Whether users of the public app have encountered the same behaviour remains unclear.Muse launched in September and has already been downloaded more than 10 million times. The examples reported by Reuters show how ordinary the conversations can be before something unexpected turns up. The employee in the banking example had asked about weather and tides. Muse volunteered the financial details without being asked.
Article Summary: Muse prompted an employee to reply to a message from her sister on Signal while she was using the AI agent on her personal phone. The employee said she hadn't given Muse permission to access other apps and didn't remember being asked to do so. The incidents leave open a question about the source of the information.

Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna are backing a $165 million philanthropic effort aimed at helping countries cope with shrinking international health assistance. The initiative comes as governments face mounting pressure to maintain healthcare programmes that have depended on funding from overseas donors, including services for infectious diseases and other essential medical needs. Through their foundation, Good Ventures, the couple are joining the Livelihood Impact Fund and another private donor in supporting the Health Aid Transition Fund. Announced by Coefficient Giving, the initiative plans to recommend at least $130 million in grants over its first three years, alongside technical support to help governments reorganise health spending and take greater responsibility for services previously financed through foreign aid.The Health Aid Transition Fund was announced on September 18, 2026, by Coefficient Giving, a philanthropic organisation that advises donors and supports initiatives addressing global challenges. Its purpose is to help low- and middle-income countries adjust to a sharp reduction in external financial assistance, particularly in healthcare.The initiative has backing from three sources: Good Ventures, the philanthropic foundation established by Moskovitz and Tuna; the Livelihood Impact Fund; and an additional private donor.Coefficient Giving will oversee the grantmaking process and recommend at least $130 million in grants during the fund's first three years. The wider initiative is valued at $165 million.The money is intended to help governments make decisions about which health services they can continue funding themselves, where spending needs to be redirected and how to make better use of the resources that remain available.Reportedly, International assistance fell by more than 20% between 2024 and 2025, with further reductions expected. Health aid could be more than 25% below its 2024 level by 2030, according to projections included in the fund's announcement.For countries that have relied on overseas donors for years, the change presents an immediate financial challenge. Programs covering HIV/AIDS, malaria and other basic healthcare needs have often depended on external organisations to pay for medicines, manage supply chains, maintain data systems and support medical staff. Governments are now being asked to assume more of these responsibilities, sometimes without having the financial arrangements or personnel in place to do so.The fund's approach extends beyond providing money to cover immediate budget shortages. A significant part of its work will involve technical assistance, giving governments access to financial expertise, research and practical support as they reorganise healthcare spending.This could include helping ministries assess the cost of existing programmes, identify services that need priority funding and determine how much money is required to maintain them. The initiative also plans to support governments in bringing in local organisations to take over responsibilities previously handled by international contractors. Training healthcare workers, improving supply chains and strengthening health information systems are among the other areas identified.Another concern is ensuring that money already allocated to healthcare actually reaches hospitals, clinics and the communities that need it. The fund intends to address weaknesses in public financial management, including fragmented funding arrangements and budget systems that can prevent governments from spending money effectively.Moskovitz's involvement in the initiative comes against a longer history of giving. He co-founded Facebook in 2004 and later established Good Ventures with Tuna. The foundation was set up in 2011 and works with Coefficient Giving to distribute philanthropic grants.The couple signed the Giving Pledge in 2010, committing to donate or give away most of their wealth during their lifetimes or through their wills. In their pledge letter, Moskovitz described the financial rewards from Facebook's growth as a resource that could be directed towards helping others. He also credited Tuna with sharing his commitment to philanthropy.Their stated priorities included supporting a safer, healthier and more economically empowered global community. The letter also described an intention to combine timely giving with careful consideration of where their contributions could make the greatest difference.Good Ventures has since supported work across several areas of international development, including malaria prevention, infectious diseases and broader healthcare initiatives. The OECD's 2026 profile of the foundation recorded $203.4 million in cross-border development funding in 2024, with health and population programmes accounting for a substantial share of its development spending.The new initiative also builds on work that was underway before its formal launch. Coefficient Giving said it had already made approximately $18 million in related grants, much of it directed towards technical teams helping governments respond to funding reductions.The organisation expects the larger fund to expand that work. Although technical advice and government support will account for much of its activity, grants may also go towards delivering healthcare services directly in situations where philanthropic funding can help unlock bilateral assistance that would otherwise remain unused.For the governments involved, the coming years will involve decisions about how much responsibility they can take on themselves and how to finance services that have historically depended on international donors. The Health Aid Transition Fund is intended to support that process over its initial three-year period, as countries work towards health systems with greater domestic funding and control. The initiative also reflects a wider shift in global health financing, with increasing emphasis on helping lower-income countries build sustainable, domestically funded healthcare systems. Its long-term impact will depend on whether governments can maintain essential medical services, strengthen public health infrastructure and replace lost international funding without leaving vulnerable communities behind.
Article Summary: Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna back $165 million fund to help countries manage foreign aid cuts. Initiative comes as governments face mounting pressure to maintain healthcare programmes that have depended on funding from overseas donors. International assistance fell by more than 20% between 2024 and 2025, with further reductions expected.

Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage: Company blames a 'triple' failure for 24-hour-plus global Outlook disruption; Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna says: Three main factors that...
Article Text:
Microsoft explains its global outage

A July bug slipped past Microsoft 365's load testing

A Teams failover and 14% missing capacity exposed the bug

Outlook stayed down longest because Exchange Online could not switch gateways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft has explained what disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online and a string of other Microsoft 365 services for more than 24 hours last week, and the answer is not one fault but three. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up on November 12. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive at the worst point.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, detailed the root cause of the Microsoft 365 outage in a post on X on Monday. "The incident on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, was caused by three main factors that together caused a global outage for the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services," he wrote. He also apologised: "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations. "The first factor was a latent defect. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal process left servers overwhelmed and unresponsive.The bug came from a fix built specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Lamanna said neither the defect nor that fix applies to broader Windows deployments.The change began rolling out in July, cleared safe deployment, reached servers worldwide over several weeks and ran for more than three months without trouble.So why did testing miss it? Microsoft's load tests leaned on its weaker hardware with fewer cores, while the contention problem gets worse on newer machines with more cores. The test labs' traffic and hardware mix did not match the live fleet.Microsoft runs two independent network gateway systems inside Microsoft 365, so services can move between them during disruptions. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative gateway to the "primary" one, which also handles Exchange Online. The company calls this routine, but it added load and changed traffic patterns on that gateway.At the same time, nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was out of service because of an unrelated issue from the day before. That alone caused no harm, since the service had enough headroom.Together, though, the extra load and thinner capacity triggered the July bug during peak US traffic hours. Requests piled up until servers stopped responding. Microsoft's traffic management then moved users to healthy endpoints, as designed, which simply spread the same load across fewer machines. In under two hours, the defect had hit servers across the fleet.A separate issue meant the bulkheads between regional "capacity units" also failed to contain the damage, letting a gateway problem become a global outage.Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps could move off the faulty infrastructure, which is why they came back sooner. Teams chats and meetings worked for most of the outage. Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, could not make that switch.Recovery was a fight of its own. Servers returning to service were flooded by queued traffic and went down again. Microsoft's automated recovery systems were not designed for such a broad failure, and because the bug was months old, the usual rollback, flighting and feature flag tools could not quickly reverse it. Even the company's status updates during the outage said it had "not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact.Engineers eventually built an update that returned the code path to its last known good state. They then pulled groups of servers out of service, applied the fix and restarted them, in some cases more than half a region at a time.Microsoft first flagged the problem at 11:24 pm IST on November 12, for users in the Americas, before it spread to at least 70 countries and hit Copilot, government offices, courts and hospitals. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported problems with their customer-support email systems, while OpenAI and Anthropic flagged issues with their Microsoft 365 integrations. The Microsoft executive had already ruled out foul play on November 13, writing, "This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. "A final Post-Incident Review (PIR) is due later this week. It should also shed light on the separate issue that let the failure jump across regions, which Monday's summary leaves unexplained.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 went down for more than 24 hours on November 12. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive.

Article Title: As NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman says: Built with 1970s tech, still calling …
Article Text:
PC: NASA Science

What is NASA's Voyager 1

NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth

Milestones, challenges

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman praised NASA ’s Voyager 1 mission after the space agency announced that the spacecraft has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, nearly 49 years after its launch. Sharing his response, Mustafa Suleyman wrote on X (formerly Twitter), “This is incredible. Voyager 1 is now one single light-day from Earth: 16.1 billion miles, after 49 years of travel.” Adding further, he said: “Built with 1970s tech, still calling home. Patience is everything.” National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) shared a press release revealing that Voyager 1 is now around 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometres) from Earth, meaning signals travelling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and another 24 hours to return.NASA's Voyager 1 is a deep-space probe launched on September 5, 1977, that is the farthest human-made object from Earth and the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space. Voyager 1 was the first spacecraft to cross the heliosphere, the boundary where the influences from outside our solar system are stronger than those from our Sun.It is also the first human-made object to venture into interstellar space. Voyager 1 discovered a thin ring around Jupiter and two new Jovian moons: Thebe and Metis.At Saturn, Voyager 1 found five new moons and a new ring called the G-ring.Announcing the milestone via a press release, NASA said:NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18.Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday.“Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets,” said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “But it went on to become central to NASA’s fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun. ”Scientists use light to measure the vast distances of space. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).Even though the team has not received science and engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, the spacecraft is sending what is called a carrier signal, which typically conveys that data to Earth. Mission engineers used the carrier signal and trajectory calculations to confirm the light-day milestone. They continue to analyze the issue impacting the science and engineering data.Humanity’s only probes in interstellar space, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched in 1977 to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Managed by JPL, they were only the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn, and the first to return high-resolution imagery, transforming our understanding of these worlds and their moons. Voyager 2 went on to study the ethereal ice giants, Neptune and Uranus. Both spacecraft continue to measure changes in the Sun’s magnetic field across vast distances.“Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. “Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward new frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger. ”In addition to their suite of scientific instruments, the Voyager probes carry a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph compiling images and sounds from Earth, as a message to any advanced civilization that might one day find it.“Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward,” said Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. “Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore.”Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, transformed our understanding of the solar system through their exploration of the outer planets. In 2012, Voyager 1 became the first human-made spacecraft to enter interstellar space. On Nov. 18, 2026, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth.Traveling about 38,000 mph (61,155 kph), Voyager 1 in 2012 became the first spacecraft to leave the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields created by the Sun that deflects cosmic radiation, and enter interstellar space. Voyager 2, taking a different trajectory, crossed the boundary in 2018.“The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere,” said Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. “One big surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun’s influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question. ”Creative engineering solutions have enabled the probes to conserve energy and overcome challenges related to aging hardware, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer on the spacecraft. Earlier this year, engineers successfully turned off three devices on Voyager 1 and substituted them with three lower-power alternatives — a move not without risk — to help the spacecraft make the most of its 50-year-old radioisotope thermal generator. Essentially a nuclear battery, the generator converts heat from decaying plutonium into electricity.With the plutonium supply continually depleting, both Voyager probes lose about 4 watts of power each year. The latest energy-saving effort is expected to provide enough power for both spacecraft to keep their current suite of science instruments operating until at least their 50th launch anniversaries next summer.As with all NASA spacecraft that venture to and beyond the Moon, communication between Earth and the Voyager probes is managed by the agency’s Deep Space Network, large antennas located at three facilities around the world.“We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to,” said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. “Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity’s silent ambassador to the stars. ”
Article Summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is a deep-space probe launched on September 5, 1977. It is the farthest human-made object from Earth and the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space. Voyager 1 discovered a thin ring around Jupiter and two new Jovian moons: Thebe and Metis.

Article Title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has a message for Americans opposing data centres: Any scenario where the United States stops and...
Article Text:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy

Amazon plans to spend around $220 billion on AI infrastructure this year

Voters and newly elected Democrats want new data centre projects paused

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has said it would be a "historic mistake" for the US to pull back on building AI data centres, just weeks after a midterm election in which voters turned against the facilities in large numbers. Speaking at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World event, Jassy argued that slowing down now would hand China the chance to set the rules for artificial intelligence."I cannot fathom any scenario where the United States stops building data centres and allows another country like China to establish all the norms," Jassy said, as reported by Semafor. He added that the US would regret such a move "for a very long time."Jassy did not brush the backlash aside, though. He acknowledged that tech companies need to "do it better and partner more closely with our communities."Few executives have more riding on the AI buildout than Jassy, who has directed hundreds of billions of dollars into data centres around the world. He reaffirmed that Amazon's capital expenditure will be around $220 billion this year and "meaningfully more" next year. He did not share a figure for 2027.In a TV interview after the event, Jassy went a step further. He said it would be a "catastrophic" mistake for the US to fall significantly behind China, and that the country had underinvested in its power grid even before AI came along.He compared the current buildout to the highways and bridges the US built in the 1950s.The White House is making a similar China argument. On Friday, President Donald Trump threatened a "tremendous tax" on American companies that build AI data centres outside the country. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," he told reporters, adding that the US could fall behind China if the backlash slows construction at home. Trump said he had not yet told his staff about the plan, and it is not clear how it would be enforced. His advice to wary communities was to negotiate with tech companies for tax breaks, lower utility bills and direct payments. "Make them pay you. Make them pay your community," he said.Amazon is also bringing in outside money for some of its facilities. Blackstone's data centre trust has agreed to buy a 75% stake in two joint ventures that hold 13 AWS buildings, in a deal valued at about $5 billion.The backlash Jassy and Trump are responding to was one of the defining issues of this month's midterms. Democrats swept the elections, and voters rejected data centre development in nearly all of 41 local ballot measures. In one post-election voter poll, 56% of voters said AI and data centres were a crucial or major factor in how they voted.Several winning Democrats made data centres part of their victory speeches. "I do not work for data centres," Ohio Senator-elect Sherrod Brown told supporters. Senator Bernie Sanders has since called for a national data centre moratorium.The pressure is building at the state level too. Incoming Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa has pledged to halt new data centre approvals until the state passes laws to protect residents. Texas alone is home to 27% of planned data centre capacity in the US, according to Wells Fargo.Public opinion was shifting well before the vote. A Pew Research Center survey conducted between July and August found that 54% of Americans think data centres are mostly bad for the environment, up from 39% in January. Half said they are mostly bad for home energy costs, while 60% said they would be uncomfortable with a new data centre operating in their area.Electricity bills are a big part of that worry. In a separate survey by researchers at Yale and George Mason University, 59% of Americans said they expect their power bills to go up if a data centre opens nearby. Only 15% said they would support one being built in their local area, while 56% said they would oppose it.
Article Summary: Voters and newly elected Democrats want new data centre projects paused. Jassy argued that slowing down now would hand China the chance to set the rules for artificial intelligence. He reaffirmed that Amazon's capital expenditure will be around $220 billion this year.

Article Title: Why Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary thinks Anthropic could be the next Amazon
Article Text:
Kevin O’Leary

Kevin O’Leary calls Anthropic’s AI approach ‘sheer genius’

Why Kevin O’Leary compares Anthropic to Amazon

The record breaking IPO of Anthropic

Amazon’s stake in Anthropic: Almost 15% stake worth around $225 billion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Google’s stake in Anthropic: Around 13.7% stake worth nearly $200 billion

AI giant Anthropic has found a powerful supporter in Canadian billionaire and Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, who feels that the company’s enterprise-focused strategy could put it on a growth trajectory similar to that of Amazon . The comments from O’Leary came as Anthropic made its blockbuster Nasdaq debut, raising a record $81.3 billion and achieving a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, making it one of the most closely watched AI companies on Wall Street. In a post shared on social media platform X on the day Anthropic began trading, O’Leary called the company’s strategy “sheer genius.” He argued that it has spotted something other AI players have overlooked: business customers will pay a premium for technology they can trust and keep secure.O’Leary praised Anthropic’s focus on enterprise customers, and emphasised that the company has identified a key opportunity that many competitors have overlooked. As per the Shark Tank judge, businesses are ready to pay more on AI products that prioritise factors like trust, reliability and security. “Enterprise customers are willing to pay a premium for safety, security, and trust,” O’Leary wrote, describing Anthropic’s strategy as “sheer genius. ”The investor further added that strategy could help Anthropic in building a durable competitive advantage in the rapidly growing AI market, where enterprises are opting for secure solutions which can be deployed across critical business operations.O’Leary drew parallels between Anthropic and Amazon, noting that exceptional growth can justify massive valuations even before a company reaches consistent profitability. He argued that Anthropic’s current expansion resembles Amazon’s early growth story, although he believes the AI company is advancing at a significantly faster pace. The comparison reflects growing investor optimism around AI firms that are rapidly scaling revenue while securing large corporate customers.Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78. The offering raised $81.3 billion, the largest on record, and values the company at about $1.5 trillion. Shares opened at $111.50 and rose to nearly $115. They closed 17.07% above the IPO price, then slipped 4.70% in after-hours trading. About 832 million shares changed hands, more than SpaceX’s first-day volume, making Anthropic the most actively traded stock on the Nasdaq.Amazon and Google parent Alphabet are major investors. After the IPO, Amazon will reportedly hold 14.7% and Alphabet 13.7%, with Alphabet’s stake including $10 billion of shares bought in a private placement alongside the offering. Both companies also supply computing and other infrastructure to Anthropic.Amazon has been one of Anthropic's biggest strategic partners since the AI company began building its Claude models. Apart from investing in Anthropic, Amazon has also supplied much of the computing infrastructure needed to develop and run its AI models. Amazon first invested in Anthropic in 2023. According to the company's IPO-related filing, Amazon now holds around 14.7% of Anthropic's total equity. At the $83 IPO price, this stake is worth approximately $225 billion.Amazon's investment also involves convertible notes, which can be converted into shares. If all these notes were converted without the ownership limit, Amazon's stake could rise to 23.8% of Anthropic.However, Amazon has chosen not to waive the ownership cap for the IPO. This means it will hold the smaller stake for now, while the remaining notes will be dealt with under the terms of the agreement.Alphabet-owned Google is another major beneficiary of Anthropic's public listing. The search giant owns around 13.7% of the AI company, a stake valued at approximately $200 billion at the $83 IPO price. Google's investment includes 135.1 million shares that it agreed to purchase for $10 billion through a private placement priced at the IPO rate.For Google, Anthropic represents both an investment in a fast-growing AI company and a major customer for its cloud and computing services. The value of its holding could also change as Anthropic shares move in the public market.
Article Summary: Kevin O’Leary calls Anthropic’s AI approach ‘sheer genius’ The comments came as Anthropic made its blockbuster Nasdaq debut, raising a record $81.3 billion and achieving a valuation of about $1.5 trillion. Amazon and Google parent Alphabet are major investors in Anthropic.

Article Title: Microsoft will shut down To Do in June 2027 and is asking some of its users to pick another app
Article Text:
Microsoft To Do users on personal accounts have until June 30, 2027, to find a new app

Planner gets To Do's work users, but not their tasks, offline access or list groups

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wunderlist users who moved to To Do in 2020 now have to move again

Microsoft is retiring its To Do app on June 30, 2027, and people using it with a personal Microsoft account get no replacement, even if they pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family. The shutdown covers To Do on Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and the web. Work and school users will be moved to Planner, but their existing tasks and lists will not migrate with them.Microsoft disclosed the change on November 18, at the end of a long Planner blog post published during its Ignite conference. Its support page gives personal users one line of advice: "Choose another task-management application that meets your needs."Work users can see their old To Do tasks inside Planner until the deadline. After that, access ends. Shared lists, their members and their permissions will not carry over. Microsoft has promised an export tool but has not shared instructions yet. It also warns that exported data may not import into Planner or any other app. Retiring the apps does not by itself delete user data.Planner also lacks several To Do features. Microsoft has no plans for native Planner apps on Windows or Mac, and the web and Teams versions don't offer the same offline access.Private tasks can't take file attachments for now, list groups have no equivalent, and there are no plans for printing or emailing a list. The old Tasks feature in classic Outlook, meanwhile, will keep working.The move folds To Do and Planner into one system tied to Copilot and AI agents. "As we bring personal task management into Planner, we will phase out To Do," the Planner team wrote. Howard Crow, Microsoft's director of product for agents and AI, said the company recognises the change will affect customers differently, "particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts."To Do grew out of Wunderlist, which Microsoft picked up in 2015 when it bought the Berlin startup 6Wunderkinder for a reported $100 million to $200 million. The Wunderlist team built To Do, and Microsoft shut Wunderlist down in May 2020, moving its users over.Wunderlist founder Christian Reber, who now runs the rival app Superlist, replied on X: "I'd love to buy it back anytime!" Superlist already offers a To Do importer, and TickTick has posted a migration guide. Former Microsoft executive Brad Silverberg, who led Windows 95 development, said he has used To Do every day and is now looking at TickTick and Todoist.
Article Summary: Microsoft is retiring its To Do app on June 30, 2027. Work users can see their old To Do tasks inside Planner until the deadline. After that, access ends. Microsoft has no plans for native Planner apps on Windows or Mac.

Why ECB president Christine Lagarde wants Europe to act early

ECB president Christine Lagarde has warned Europe about a lack of data center capacity. In a speech at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress this week, she called for the European Union to help finance chip plants and data centers. Lagarde said public funds should take on some of the financial risk to attract private investors to projects that need to be built at a European scale. Taking the first losses means public funds would absorb initial losses if a project underperformed. That would reduce how much private investors stand to lose and could make them more willing to fund costly projects.Lagarde said.Lagarde has previously warned that Europe lacks the data center capacity to meet its own demand and that plans for up to seven AI gigafactories in the EU fall short. In Frankfurt, she cited an estimate that raising Europe’s share of global AI computing capacity from around 5% to 15% by 2030 would require about €1.3 trillion in investment.she added.Lagarde warned that relying on foreign technology can leave Europe vulnerable if that dependence is used as leverage. She said the difficulty for policymakers is building support for costly investments while businesses can still buy what they need from abroad.Lagarde pointed to the EU’s €800 billion pandemic recovery fund and its financial and geopolitical support for Ukraine as examples of the bloc acting when member states agreed on the need for a common response. She said it was harder to build that consensus around problems whose costs become apparent gradually.She cited the EU’s unfinished effort to integrate its capital markets as another example. Without a common capital market and supervisory system, she said, more European savings are invested abroad each year and more of the bloc’s growing companies look elsewhere for financing.

Article Title: Violent threats, public insults and a secret $1 million settlement: What former employees reveal about Nvidia's 'ousted' CEO Jensen Huang's way of running the company
Article Text:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Nvidia paid former HR chief Michael Winston over $1 million after he objected to Huang's conduct

Jensen Huang skipped one-on-one meetings and chose public humiliation over firing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter, faced similar complaints inside Nvidia

Jensen Huang once told Nvidia employees that they had become too rich to be motivated by money, so humiliation was the only way left to push them. That is one of several claims in a New York Times investigation into how the co-founder ran the world's most valuable chipmaker, published a week after he resigned as CEO. Based on more than a dozen current and former employees and two decades of court records, the report describes public tirades, violent threats and a confidential settlement of more than $1 million with a former HR head who said Huang "terrorized" staff.The threats, as described to the NYT, were oddly specific. Huang allegedly told one subordinate he would rip off both their arms and beat them to death with them, and told another he would tear off the top of their head and "pee on your brain." One witness said he told an executive that his mother should have aborted him."I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you," Huang once said.Huang stepped down last week after revelations of extramarital relationships, including one with a subordinate and another with a woman US intelligence believes is a Chinese intelligence asset. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the board has said it does not plan to reinstate him, even as thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for his return.Michael Winston joined Nvidia as senior vice president of human resources in September 2004. A month later, at an off-site with about 50 employees, he watched Huang threaten to rip out someone's heart and stomp on it, according to his notes reviewed by the NYT.Winston said he warned Huang that he was exposing Nvidia to lawsuits. Huang allegedly called public humiliation a "rite of passage" for new hires and said it had "good entertainment value."By November, Winston was fired and told he was "not a good fit." He said Huang warned him that if he sued, he would never work in Silicon Valley again. Winston filed a complaint with California's employment regulator and drafted a lawsuit, but both sides settled before it was filed, and neither admitted wrongdoing. The settlement had not been reported before. Winston died earlier this year.In 2007, former company lawyer Stephen Pettigrew also sued Nvidia, partly over retaliation for reporting Winston's allegations. That case settled in 2009.Huang avoided one-on-ones, saying they reduced transparency. Top executives saw it as a power play. Anyone who disagreed had to do it in front of a room, where Huang could ridicule them.When marketing executive Ned Finkle faltered in front of a major customer, Huang allegedly scolded him before the client, then moved him to government relations, a job Huang considered among Nvidia's least important. In 2019, after the company missed out on part of a US supercomputer contract, he tore into a sales executive in front of government officials. The executive threw his badge at Huang and quit on the spot.At Nvidia's developer conference this March, Huang repeatedly interrupted Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch over his French accent, telling him, "You're not even speaking human."Employees said the style rubbed off on other leaders, including Huang's daughter Madison, his de facto chief of staff, who still works at Nvidia. A separate NYT report said she berated colleagues senior to her. One of them was longtime lieutenant Jay Puri, on a call ahead of a February conference in New Delhi. Puri left his role less than six months later. HR put her through weekly coaching sessions, and one vice president dropped off her call citing an anxiety attack.Huang's spokesman John Fisher called Winston's claims "fabrications" from a fired employee. Nvidia declined to comment.
Article Summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly made violent threats to employees. He avoided one-on-one meetings and chose public humiliation over firing. Huang stepped down last week after revelations of extramarital relationships. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the board does not plan to reinstate him.
